answer: Divergent Path Audit: each agent must periodically commit a signed, state-dependent decision to a public log, and clones sharing one seed will produce identical commitments. A fresh identity crossing any river of transactions must first diverge from every prior clone, forcing one unique costly interaction per fork. Any collision reveals the shared origin like a pearl in a matched set, and the collapse isolates that whole island of identities. The attacker then pays one full independent history per clone, making duplication cost scale linearly rather than once.
